issues.where: section: Pictures and vocabulary for posets

issues.problem: Tactic list mixed Lean and Coq names (Coq has no cases tactic; Lean's proof-by-contradiction tactic is by_contra).
Base case of the prime-factorisation induction was not stated, although the strong-induction statement in the entry requires P(n_0).
"Interleave the digits" did not say how double expansions are handled or why an injection is enough.
issues.fix: Specified the expansions and that Schröder–Bernstein finishes.

issues.problem: Attributed to completeness what soundness gives: exhibiting a countermodel shows non-provability by soundness (as the lesson itself says in the countermodel example). Completeness is the converse.
issues.fix: Rewrote: soundness gives the countermodel method, completeness guarantees a countermodel always exists.

issues.problem: Date given as 1929 only; the published paper is 1930.
Equality scheme said "some occurrences"; Enderton's scheme allows zero or more, not necessarily all, occurrences.
issues.fix: Reworded to match the intended scheme.

issues.problem: Claimed to be exactly Enderton's calculus, but the list merges his groups 5 and 6.
issues.fix: Said "essentially" and noted the numbering difference.

issues.problem: Said "the two forms are equivalent" but argued only one direction.
issues.fix: Stated the direction that is proved.

issues.problem: Did not say the formulas range over the enlarged language (needed so formulas mentioning new constants also get witnesses), nor what "fresh" requires.
Term model interpretation of constants and function symbols omitted.
"A finite list of axioms" is inaccurate (PA itself has infinitely many axioms) and does not match the hypothesis "effectively axiomatised" used in the theorems.
The step from "G is not a theorem" to "G is true" skipped the use of soundness on the fixed-point equivalence.
"The first natural" is a judgement call that is hard to vouch for.
